Using the New Call Center Phone Menu
Oct 14, 2026
As
previously communicated

Gabby can assist with five common inquiry types:
Claim Status
Prior Authorizations
Member Eligibility
Payments
Provider Enrollment

Please have this information ready before you call so that you can quickly provide it to Gabby. Gabby will prompt multiple times for the information it needs to proceed. If you do not provide a valid response, Gabby will disconnect.

Federally Required MaineCare Off-Cycle Provider Revalidation Plan: October 2026 Update

Oct 13, 2026

As previously communicated, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) requested all states develop and submit a comprehensive two-year provider revalidation strategy, with priority given to revalidating high-risk providers. 

You can find Maine’s two-year plan and a list of all providers included in the off-cycle revalidation on the Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) Federally Required 2026-2028 Off-Cycle Revalidation Plan webpage. OMS grouped providers into five cohorts and sends notices alerting providers at least 30 days prior to initiating the revalidation window for their assigned cohort. OMS additionally sends a 60-day post-initiation notice, per standard revalidation practices.

Milestones to note:

Cohorts 1 & 2: Individual high-risk providers, providers without an NPI, Personal Care Agencies, Home Health Agencies, Hospice, and Assisted Living Services providers

  • On July 19, 2026, OMS mailed a 30-day notice to impacted providers in Cohorts 1 and 2 announcing that their revalidation window would open on August 17, 2026.
  • Providers in Cohorts 1 and 2 who do not submit a revalidation case by Friday October 16, 2026, will have claims pend until they submit their revalidation case.
  • Providers who miss the October 16th deadline will have until November 16, 2026, to submit their revalidation case. Any provider who has not submitted a required revalidation case by that date will be terminated effective November 17, 2026.

You can find more information about the provider revalidation process on our Provider Enrollment and Revalidation webpage.

Questions?

For questions about this off-cycle revalidation process, please email Kenneth Jamison, Provider Enrollment Manager. For general assistance with the revalidation process, please contact the Provider Services Call Center at 1-866-690-5585, Option 7 for Revalidation Questions, or email MaineCare Enrollment.

The Department remains committed to program integrity, responsible stewardship, and clear communication with providers throughout this process. We will continue to share information with providers through usual communication channels as appropriate.

The MaineCare Third Party Liability (TPL) Exemption Request and Attestation Form is Now Available

Oct 13, 2026

On August 3, 2026, MaineCare announced claims system updates to support proper TPL reimbursement processes in accordance with MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM), Chapter I, Section 1.07 TPL rules. The MaineCare TPL Exemption Request and Attestation Form is now available for TPL exemption request submission.  

Requesting TPL Exemption 

In accordance with MBM, Chapter I, Section 1.07 rules, MaineCare may assess the validity of extenuating circumstance or service code TPL exemption requests to bill MaineCare as the primary payer for services delivered to a member with primary, public, or commercial coverage. Providers wishing to apply for TPL exemption to bill MaineCare as the primary payer must complete and submit the MaineCare TPL Exemption Request and Attestation Form to the TPL Medicare Code Exempt Request email box.  

MaineCare will review completed forms with the supporting documentation and provide a decision letter of approval or non-approval via email to the requestor. An exemption request approval letter is valid only for a specific member for a defined duration, no greater than 12 months. The exemption request approval letter must be attached to all applicable MaineCare claims for dates of service during the approved time. Claims without a valid and up-to-date approval letter may result in denials.  

Providers are responsible for maintaining exemption request renewals by submitting a subsequent MaineCare TPL Exemption Request and Attestation Form at least 30 calendar days prior to the expiration date specified in the approval letter.  

Limited Retroactive TPL Exemption Review Period 

For a limited time, MaineCare will consider continuity of care retroactive exemption requests with supporting documentation for claims directly impacted by the system updates announced in the Provider Responsibility Regarding Third Party Liability and Secondary Billing e-message we sent on August 3, 2026.  

After December 31, 2026, retroactive exemption requests may not be accepted for review. Providers who receive retroactive exemption request approvals may resubmit their claims with the applicable approval letter attached for claims processing. 

For questions, please contact your Provider Relations Specialist.

System Remittance Advice (RA) and 835 Limitations

Oct 13, 2026

Attention Nursing Homes, Hospitals, and Private Non-Medical Institutions, Appendix C & F (PNMI-C-F): Claims RA/835 Issues

Following the MIHMS upgrade, there are open issues affecting some RA/835s.  The issues are high priority for a fix that is underway; we are currently targeting to fix the issues by the end of October and will send another communication when the issues have been resolved. This message provides details of the issues and available workarounds until the issues are fixed. 

Cost of Care Reporting for Nursing Home, Hospital Claims, and PNMI-C-F 

Nursing Home and Hospital claims for members with cost of care are not being reported with the appropriate Claim Adjustment Reason Code (CARC) needed for balance billing members. 

  • PDF RA – CARC 142 is not being reported for cost of care. 
  • 835 – CARC 96 is being reported in error. 

As a workaround until the fix is in place, MaineCare will provide a report that can be accessed on the MaineCare Partner Portal. On the Dashboard, navigate to Reports > Other Reports > “Cost of Care Report.” This report will be available on Mondays for the claims finalized on the prior Wednesday. Because this week’s claims will be finalized on Thursday, the first report will be available no later than Tuesday, October 20, 2026.  

Spenddown Reporting for Provider Claims 

Claims with spenddown are not being reported with the appropriate CARC needed for balance billing members. 

  • PDF RA – CARC 142 is not being reported for spenddown claims.   
  • 835 – CARC 96 and/or CARC 178 is being reported in error. 

As a workaround until the fix is in place, MaineCare will provide a report that can be accessed on the MaineCare Partner Portal. On the dashboard, navigate to Reports > Other Reports > “Spend Down Report.” This report will be available on Mondays for the claims finalized on the prior Wednesday. Because this week’s claims will be finalized on Thursday, the first report will be available no later than Tuesday, October 20, 2026.  

Hospital Crossover Claims 

Hospital crossover claims are not reporting the correct CARC when the member has Medicare and full MaineCare coverage, and the claim balance is for deductible or coinsurance.  In this situation, you would normally expect a B1 CARC. 

  • PDF RA – CARC B1 is being reported appropriately. 
  • 835 – CARC 45 is being reported in error. 

As a one-time workaround, MaineCare will provide a report after this issue has been resolved. On the dashboard, navigate to Reports > Other Reports > “Bad Debt Write off Report.” We anticipate this report will be available by November 13, 2026, and will confirm once the issue is resolved. 

Claims Processed in Excess of Charges 

Claims processed in excess of billed charges are not being reported with the appropriate CARC. 

  • PDF RA – Reporting CARC 94 appropriately. 
  • 835 – Claims that pay more than the billed amount (i.e. FQHC, Hospitals with APC, DRGs) are reporting CARC 45 instead of CARC 94. 

MaineCare does not have a workaround for this issue, as CARC 45 and CARC 94 share the same Claim Adjustment Group Code of CO (Contractual Obligation). MaineCare can provide a report upon request; please contact your Provider Relations Specialist.  

For questions, please contact Provider Services at 1-866-690-5585.

Attention Trading Partners: the MaineCare Partner Portal is Live

Oct 12, 2026

As an update to previous communications, we have launched the new MaineCare Partner Portal, which replaces the previous HealthPAS Online Portal. The MaineCare Partner Portal is now available for all regular functions, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.  

As a reminder, starting today, we are also changing how callers interact with and experience Provider Services and Member Services call center phone menus, known as Interactive Voice Response (IVR). A virtual assistant, called Gabby, will replace traditional phone menus by listening to what callers say to resolve simple inquiries. 

This message includes information you will need to get started in the MaineCare Partner Portal. The link to the MaineCare Partner Portal has not changed: mainecare.maine.gov. 

For all information about the upcoming changes to MIHMS, see the MaineCare Partner Portal section of the Provider Resources page. Please note that we have updated the FAQ previously shared, as of September 21, 2026. For information about the claims submission deadlines for the October 15, 2026 and October 21, 2026, payment cycles, please refer to the FAQ.

  2. Set up a Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) method. 
  3. Sign into MaineCare’s Partner Portal. 
  4. Invite additional (delegated) users and assign permissions as appropriate. Refer to the MaineCare Partner Portal Overview User Guide in the MMIS Learning Center.

All other (delegated) users 

  1. Please contact your Admin (R7) user if you have not received an invitation to the MaineCare Partner Portal. You will receive an email link to register. This email will come from MEMMISDoNotReply@gainwelltechnologies.com. 
  2. Enter your invitation verification code, create a password, and set up an MFA method.

Customers with questions about this discount should contact their electric company directly.

I've also called on Congress to increase funding for federal home heating assistance, and I thank Maine's congressional delegation for their bipartisan support for LIHEAP funding, despite the president's attempts to eliminate this program. And that's just not enough, though, to make up for the skyrocketing costs driven by tariffs and the president's war. Congress must ensure the safety and comfort of Maine people heading into this winter season by increasing LIHEAP funding.

In the meantime, MaineHousing has distributed about $4 million to heating fuel companies for some of our most vulnerable households, those with older adults on small incomes or small children. Those trucks will begin delivering fuel to those homes over the next few days. We're also talking to farmers and foresters and other entities that use diesel fuel a lot about other ways we might be able to help them address high diesel prices here in Maine.

I'm proud to say that thanks to our investments over the years in energy efficiency and clean energy, our reliance on heating oil has fallen from 70 percent of Maine households in 2010 to just over 50 percent now. Still, it's not enough. My administration will continue to make it as affordable as possible to transition to clean energy sources like heat pumps, to save people money, and to make sure we're not left to shoulder the burden of the president's blunders.

Are you interested in exploring heat pumps or using wood or propane to heat your home instead of oil and kerosene? Are you curious about energy assistance programs? Weatherization? Do you need contact information for local community action agencies or MaineHousing or Efficiency Maine Trust? Our Winter Heating Guide, published every year by the Maine Department of Energy Resources, has all that information, as well as some helpful tips about winterizing and saving money, and about contact information, and links to online resources. You can view and download that Winter Heating Guide and review the latest heating fuel prices at Maine.gov/Energy.

This crisis affects all of us – low income, middle income, everyone who has a home, everyone who has a bill to pay this winter. But as the weather continues to get colder, I encourage all Maine people to see how they might save money and stay warm through the winter by using our current Maine Winter heating guide found at Maine.gov/Energy.

This is Governor Janet Mills. Please stay warm, and thank you for listening.

The Maine Judicial Branch announced today that District and Superior Courts in Lincoln, Knox, Sagadahoc, and Waldo counties (comprising Judicial Region 6) will transition from paper filing to electronic filing (eFiling) on Monday, December 7, 2026. All case types in the Lincoln, Knox, Sagadahoc and Waldo County Unified Criminal Dockets (UCDs) and Superior Courts; and in the Belfast, Rockland, West Bath, and Wiscasset District Courts will transition to eFiling. Region 6 Will Be the Second to Last Judicial Region to Complete the Transition to eFiling
When Region 6 courts transition to eFiling on December 7, they will be the second-to-last judicial region to implement eFiling. Earlier this year, courts in Judicial Regions 2, 7, 8, 1, and 4 made the switch from paper filing to eFiling. The Maine Judicial Branch remains on track to have all courts on the new system by February 2027.

Supreme Judicial Court Chief Justice Valerie Stanfill noted, "We are pleased that the transition from paper filing to eFiling has proceeded so smoothly this year, a testament to the hard work and dedication of all Judicial Branch staff. The eCourts project implementation and project support teams have traveled all over the state to make the transition successful, and they certainly deserve special acknowledgement."

Who Is Required to eFile?
Attorneys, government agencies (except law enforcement agencies), and parties who file more than six non-emergency cases in a calendar year, are required to eFile in courts that have implemented Maine eCourts. Self-represented parties are not required to eFile and can continue to file documents as they always have, in paper at the courthouse, by mail, or by email if filing a protection from abuse or harassment case.

About Maine eCourts
Maine eCourts is a suite of applications and web-based tools provided by Tyler Technologies' Enterprise Justice Software. The system allows for the management of court dockets and hearings, storage of digital case files, eFiling, and online payments.

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Contact: Danna Hayes

Danna.hayes@maine.gov

If You Bought Certain Generic Prescription Drugs in the United States Between May 2009 and December 2019, You Could be Eligible for Money

AUGUSTA – Attorney General Aaron M. Frey today joined a coalition of 45 states and territories seeking court approval of three settlements with Ascend Laboratories, Citron Pharma and Mayne Pharma to resolve allegations that the generic drug manufacturers engaged in a widespread, long-running conspiracy to artificially inflate and manipulate prices, reduce competition, and unreasonably restrain trade with regard to numerous generic prescription drugs.

Ascend will pay $400,000 to the states. Mayne will pay $650,000. Citron’s settlement only includes non-monetary terms as it has ceased business operations. As part of the settlement, the companies each agreed to meaningful injunctive terms including a series of internal reforms to ensure fair competition and compliance with antitrust laws. 

These latest settlements come as the States prepare for the first trial to be held in Hartford, Connecticut in February 2027.  

The States previously reached settlements with Sandoz, Glenmark, Lannett, Bausch, Apotex, Heritage, and Heritage’s parent company, Emcure, totaling $496.5 million.

If you purchased a generic prescription drug between May 2009 and December 2019, you may be eligible for compensation. To determine your eligibility, call 1-866-290-0182 (Toll-Free), email info@AGGenericDrugs.com or visit www.AGGenericDrugs.com. You can submit a claim for compensation.

Connecticut is leading a coalition of nearly all states and territories engaged in a series of antitrust cases, starting first in 2016. The first Complaint included Heritage and 17 other corporate Defendants, two individual Defendants, and 15 generic drugs. Two former executives from Heritage Pharmaceuticals, Jeffery Glazer and Jason Malek, have since entered into settlement agreements and are cooperating. The second Complaint was filed in 2019 against Teva Pharmaceuticals and 21 of the nation’s largest generic drug manufacturers. The Complaint names 16 individual senior executive Defendants. The third complaint, to be tried first, focuses on 80 topical generic drugs that account for billions of dollars of sales in the United States and names 26 corporate defendants and 10 individual defendants. The States filed a fourth complaint earlier this year, alleging that Novartis AG, Sandoz Group AG and Sandoz AG, are liable for Sandoz’s alleged conduct and for fraudulently transferring assets.

The cases all stem from a series of investigations built on evidence from several cooperating witnesses at the core of the different conspiracies, a massive document database of more than 20 million documents, and a phone records database containing millions of call detail records and contact information for more than 600 sales and pricing individuals in the generics industry. Each complaint addresses a different set of drugs and defendants and lays out an interconnected web of competing industry executives that met with each other during industry dinners, "girls’ nights out," lunches, cocktail parties, golf outings, and communicated via frequent telephone calls, emails, and text messages that sowed the seeds for their illegal agreements. Throughout the complaints, defendants use terms like "fair share," "playing nice in the sandbox," and "responsible competitor" to describe how they unlawfully discouraged competition, raised prices, and enforced an ingrained culture of collusion. Among the records obtained by the States is a two-volume notebook containing the contemporaneous notes of one of the States’ cooperators that memorialized his discussions during phone calls with competitors and internal company meetings over a period of several years.

States and territories also joining the settlements include: Alaska, Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, the District of Columbia, Florida, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Montana, Nebraska, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Puerto Rico, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, West Virginia, Wisconsin, and Wyoming.

The Maine Department of Education has released updated Joint IEP Guidance to help schools follow federal and state requirements. The updated guidance was developed through a collaborative effort and is available on the MaineCare in Education web page. 

DOE first released the Joint Guidance on August 28, 2026, and has re-issued this guidance effective September 18, 2026. The reissued guidance replaces the previously issued Joint Guidance and provides clarification in response to questions and feedback received from School Administrative Units (SAUs), providers, and other interested parties. 

All IEP documents must reflect the updated guidance as soon as possible, but no later than thirty (30) days of the issuance of the guidance. 

Providers with current prior authorizations for School Health-Related Services through Acentra should upload any updated documentation to Atrezzo. Acentra will accept IEP language from both versions through October 18, 2026. Beginning October 19, 2026, Acentra will only accept IEP language from the new version re-issued on September 18, 2026. 

For technical assistance regarding the billing and processing of MaineCare claims, please contact your Provider Relations Specialist. 

For all other questions related to the provision of MaineCare School Health-Related Services, please contact Trista Collins, State Medicaid Educational Liaison.    

For technical information related to IEP development, please contact Dan Hemdal at the Maine Department of Education.

items.title: Energy Conservation Program: Test Procedures for Commercial Warm Air Furnaces
items.content_text: The Department of Energy ("DOE" or "the Department") is withdrawing the test procedure for commercial warm air furnaces adopted under the Energy Policy and Conservation Act, specifically appendix B, "Uniform Test Method for Measurement of the Energy Efficiency of Commercial Warm Air Furnaces (Thermal Efficiency Two)." Upon reconsideration, DOE has determined that appendix B would have an uncertain increase in representativeness that does not outweigh the likely increase in burden. DOE has also determined that withdrawing the appendix B test procedure would be consistent with the proposed Process Rule, which states that for certain categories of equipment, including CWAFs, DOE will adopt the industry test procedure, as contemplated by EPCA, except in very limited circumstances. Commercial warm air furnaces will continue to be subject to the testing requirements of appendix A, "Uniform Test Method for Measurement of the Energy Efficiency of Commercial Warm Air Furnaces (Thermal Efficiency)."
